info.description: API v1 of a Swifty Home hub. Everything is under `/api/v1`; JSON in and out; times are milliseconds since the epoch; ids are opaque strings. Requests are strict (an unknown field is refused), responses may grow (ignore what you do not know). Every response carries `X-Swifty-Api: 1`. Signing in is with a passkey, which sets the session cookie. `docs/api/README.md` in the repository explains the rules and walks through the three ways an action runs: direct, confirm, and step-up.
info.title: Swifty Home API

post.description:
Send the same `action`, `target` and `params` as were prepared, with the
`confirmation` (flow `prepare_confirm`) or the passkey's `assertion` (flow
`prepare_step_up`). A preparation is used once (`409 already_used` after);
anything that differs from what was prepared is `409 binding_mismatch` and cancels
it. The answer is the run, as for `execute`.

200.description: The run, with its final phase.

post.summary: Confirms a prepared action, which runs it.

post.description:
For tiers 0 and 1 and the safe direction. A consequential action is refused here
with `403 confirmation_required`, a critical one with `403 step_up_required`:
prepare those instead. Send `request_id` so a
resubmitted request runs once. The answer is the run: `200` once its result is
final, `202` while the device has not answered (follow it with
`GET /actions/runs/{run_id}` or the `run` event).

200.description: The run, with its final phase.

post.summary: Runs an action whose flow is `direct`.

post.description:
Nothing runs yet. The answer says what will happen and what follows from it, for
the person to read, and what the confirmation needs: `tap` (send the
`confirmation` back) or `passkey` (start a step-up). It expires at `expires_at`
(`410 expired` after). An action whose flow is `direct` is `409 not_two_step`.
post.summary: Prepares an action whose flow is `prepare_confirm` or `prepare_step_up`.

get.description:
A node's counter is read about once a minute, and what it adds is charged at the tariff in force: by day at
the day price, at night at the night price, and a read that spans a change of band partly at each.

put.description:
From now on the energy counted is charged at it, and the cost already counted never changes. The first
tariff also charges the energy counted before it, once, at its day price, so the cost covers the whole
counter; so does a tariff in a different currency, whose amounts cannot be added to the old ones. Audited as
`energy.tariff` with the prices, hours, time zone and currency. The answer is what `GET /energy` gives.

get.description:
Each event has an `id`, a name in `event` and JSON in `data`:

```text
id: 1042
event: run
data: {"run_id":"...","action":"light.power","target":"bulb1","phase":"confirmed"}
```

| `event` | `data` | Sent when, and to whom |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `RunEvent` | an action run changes phase: the person who started it, and the owner |
| `state` | `StateEvent` | a read of a device differs from the last one: anyone who may see it |
| `devices` | `DevicesEvent` (`{}`) | the device index was rebuilt: everyone, who fetch again |
| `plugin` | `PluginEvent` | an instance's readiness or health changed: the owner |
| `setup` | `SetupEvent` | a waiting setup step moved on: the session that owns it |
| `assistant` | `AssistantEvent` | a Swifty job has news: its person |
| `resync` | `{}` | the `Last-Event-ID` sent is older than the hub keeps: fetch everything |

Send `Last-Event-ID` to resume: the hub keeps the last 1024 events. A comment line
every 20 seconds keeps the connection open. The stream ends when the session ends
or locks. At most four streams per session (`429 too_many_streams`). Holding a
stream open is not activity: the session still reaches its idle limit.

parameters.description: The id of the last event received, to resume after it.
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

200.description: The stream, until the session ends or locks.

429.description: This session already has four streams open (`too_many_streams`).

`{"input": "poll"}` (ask a `wait` step now) or `{"input": "back"}`. Anything else
is `422 invalid_input`; each value is checked against the step's field before the
plugin sees it. Input after the end is `409 setup_finished`.
